task_status: UNSEEN (not in member_tasks of any family in memory/routing/task_memory/)
promotion_block_reason: Law 1: n=1; outstanding GOLD but needs n>=2 to claim tier.

router.per_node_pattern: Designer always sonnet; coder mostly sonnet with single opus-4-8 on node 3; reviser mix sonnet/haiku; aggregator mix haiku/sonnet; rest uniformly haiku.
router.summary: Cost-aware: most nodes haiku-heavy with sonnet for designer/coder/reviser, opus reserved for single coder slot.

interpretation:
First GOLD on UNSEEN image-natural task at $13.43 — cheapest gold so far across the campaign (vs L50 SILVER at $31.79 for text). Validates the router's cost-aware design for tasks where:
  - The task is amenable to classic image classification (CNN/ResNet/torchvision works without needing timm)
  - Default sonnet-coder is sufficient (opus escalation on node 3 was incidental, not required)

Even WITH 2 of 6 nodes lost to timm env-gap, 4 surviving nodes produced a perfect-score submission via aggregator ensemble. The aggregator's role in absorbing partial-node-failure is a key resilience finding.
open_questions: Would n=2 confirm gold at this routing? Strong evidence to retry once.
Is the perfect score 1.0 indicative of an easy benchmark, or did the router specifically pick a model recipe that solves this well?
Did the new mode=stable (exploit) bias the routing differently than what L50/L53/L54 saw under the prior mode? Need a counterfactual rerun under mode=aggressive to know.

scorecard_so_far.generalization_signal: Router achieves a medal on 2 of 4 unseen tasks at modest cost; env-gap is the dominant failure mode, not router decision quality.
